derivation: Normal: every unstable entry targets a stable one. Stable z: 00 has 4=1; 01 has 1=1, 2=0; 10 has 2=1, 3=0; 11 has 2=1. Direct conflicts are {1,2} (in 01) and {2,3} (in 10).
Implied: {1,3} in 10 goes to {2,3}; {2,4} in 01 goes to {2,1}. {1,4} and {3,4} imply only identical or singleton pairs, because 4 is unspecified in 10. So the maximal compatibles are {1,4},{2},{3,4}.
Γ({1,4}) and Γ({3,4}) are empty, so they dominate their singletons. The primes are {1,4},{2},{3,4}, which is also the unique minimum closed cover; state 4 is in two members.

Tie-break (§9.6): class {2} in 00 implies {4}, which is not in {2} and is contained in both {1,4} and {3,4}. Canonical order picks {1,4}, giving entry '1,-' rather than '3,-'. The reset state 4 is also in both, and the first member containing it, {1,4}, is stable in 00, giving reset (1,00).

Class 1 = {1,4}: 00 is stable with z=1 (from member 4), 01 is stable with z=1 (from member 1), and 10 and 11 imply {2}, giving '2,-'. Class 3 = {3,4}: 00 is stable with z=1, 01 goes to class 1, 10 is stable with z=0 (member 3), 11 goes to class 2.
